title: Favorite drummers and Rene's rhythm style on the sock cymbal
summary: Rene names favorite drummers, including Alfred Williams, and describes his own steady rhythm style and accents on the sock cymbal.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Who were some of your favorite drummers?

Faiso, Shawnee, Red Haffer. Well, I was in that reading class. Me, Cantrell, and Alfred Williams. That was a nice orchestra drummer. Good reader, huh? I don't know about his reading ability, but I know for playing track drummer, he played nice snare drum, he had a nice sweep. That Sam Morgan band had a nice sweep. They didn't play too loud. He had a nice, nice band. He played nice drum, kept nice time. He was none of them felt. He made his explosion and he kept right at his time. That's what he did. Well, I was a rhythm drum player. Just rhythm. Just kept that rhythm. In my sock, I tried to pop it just clearly. It gave good, powerful accents, you see. I keep the fella right in the groove, man. He can make anything he want.
That's when your foot you'd make those accents.
Yeah, yeah. On that sock, you see. See, one, see that and, or one, two, you see. One, two, three. That's where they're at, the two and the four. On your sock cymbal?
Yeah, yeah. So you had a sock cymbal and a bass drum, both of them?
Yeah, a sock cymbal and a bass drum, yeah. Both of them. That's where they used to play, you know.
